name: SMAP
note: Soil Moisture Active Passive maps global soil moisture and freeze/thaw state every 2-3 days. Its L-band radar failed in 2015; the radiometer continued.
source: NASA/JPL SMAP launch press kit (mass 944 kg, power 1,450 W, 685 km SSO, 3-year prime mission).

name: Landsat 9
note: Landsat 9 extends the 50-year land-imaging record with 30 m multispectral imagery and an 8-day combined revisit with Landsat 8.
source: NASA Science Landsat 9 mission page (705 km, 99-minute orbit, 5-year design life); NASA fast facts (2,710 kg), WMO OSCAR (4,300 W).

name: GPM Core Observatory
note: GPM Core carries a dual-frequency precipitation radar and a microwave imager, flying at 65 degrees inclination to sample rain and snow worldwide.
source: NASA GPM mission page and 2014 press kit (3,850 kg, 1,950 W, 407 km, 65 degrees, 3-year design life).

name: NISAR
note: NISAR's dual L- and S-band radars scan nearly all land and ice twice every 12 days, with an average revisit of about 6 days.
source: NASA NISAR mission overview (747 km, 98.4 degrees, 12-day repeat, 3-year prime mission); NASA/JPL quick facts (about 2,380 kg, about 5 kW).
